Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 70, English)
Third Eye Batch 3: The 1 1-Day Sadhna Induction, Second Charan Jaap, and the Path of Maryada Purushottam Ram

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn induction session for the thir d batch of the "Thir d Eye" pr ogram, opening with extended Sitaram chanting, followed by Bhaiya's induction addr ess (explaining the seriousness and strictness of this level), a detailed walkthr ough of the 1 1-day sadhna's practical rules and the second-charan jaap method, and an extensive live Q&A session addr essing individual practitioners' practical questions. This session contains extensive live interaction thr oughout, so it is pr ocessed as a full 3-part document.
1. Session Context: The Third Batch of the Third Eye Pr ogram

This session explicitly opens the third batch of Ashaeiynn's "Third Eye" program, in which mentors identify and put forward practitioners whose drishti (spiritual sight) is ready for further , more intensive work. Bhaiya notes that participants in this batch may additionally gain access to further specialized vidya if they choose to pursue it.
2. Why This Level Is Unusually Strict

Bhaiya explains that he is deliberately far stricter with this batch than with general practitioners, for a specific reason: everyone in this batch already knows how Ashaeiynn functions, already understands how its shaktis work, has already completed foundational jaap, and has already begun realizing divine tattva and shakti within themselves. Because of this, there is no more room for excuses, hesitation, or "why can't I do this" conversations — at this stage, a practitioner either opens their drishti and continues forward, or steps back, with no middle ground tolerated.
3. No Turning Back Is Acceptable

Bhaiya states plainly that turning back at this stage, after having already received this much training and this much attention from sants, would make a practitioner "nalayak" (unworthy) in the most direct sense — and that he will not allow that outcome. The only direction from here is forward.
4. The 1 1-Day Commitment (Sankalp)

Bhaiya will personally take each practitioner's sankalp (vow) for an 1 1-day training period. Anyone who knows they will be busy during this period, or cannot commit to the requirements, is told to leave now or join a future batch instead — there is no partial participation.
5. The Promise Behind This Strictness

Bhaiya explains that once sankalp is taken, shakti will be specifically invoked and sent to stand ready for each practitioner , day and night, throughout the 1 1 days — for every genuine requirement, whether jaap, havan, or any other vidhi (ritual procedure). In exchange,

practitioners are expected to genuinely follow through; failing to do so after such intensive shakti has been dedicated on their behalf is treated as a serious matter , since it disrespects the ef fort of the invoked shaktis themselves.
6. Minimum Daily Practice: Four Hours of Seated Jaap

The core daily requirement is a minimum of four hours of jaap, done strictly in a seated postur e — not while walking or moving about. Practitioners may split the four hours into shorter blocks (for example, one-hour segments with breaks) if needed, but each segment must be done seated, with a lit lamp (diya) placed in front of them.
7. The Physical Setup for the Sadhna

The practical setup requires: a photo of Prabhu (to be provided), placed before a lit diya; tilak applied by the practitioner's own hand, with rice (chawal) added, and chandan, itr , or flowers optional; the practitioner should sit either on an asan or directly on the ground, according to their own preference. Per this teaching, the specific combination of one's own body , the tilak, the rice, and the earth beneath is described as an essential elemental combination for this sadhna.
8. Looking Into Prabhu's Eyes While Chanting

Practitioners are instructed to gaze into the eyes of Prabhu's photo while chanting — not as a forced, unblinking trataka-style stare, but a natural, repeated returning of the gaze to Prabhu's eyes whenever the eyes are open, alternating with closing the eyes to focus inward.
9. Rules for the Sadhna Space
The specific spot used for this sadhna should not be used by anyone else, and should be kept clean by the practitioner personally — not delegated to household help — for the duration of the 1 1 days.
10. Sleeping on the Gr ound, and Why

Practitioners are required to sleep on the ground (a mattress placed directly on the floor is acceptable) rather than on a raised bed, for the 1 1-day period. Per this teaching, this is done specifically out of respect toward visiting sants: sants who visit and touch a sleeping practitioner do so when that practitioner is sleeping at ground level; they do not disturb practitioners sleeping on an elevated bed.
1 1. Combining With Siya Tattva Sadhna

For practitioners also doing Siya Tattva sadhna, Bhaiya notes this combination works especially well — since Siya Tattva sadhna already primes/binds the practitioner's bodily elements in a way that aligns with what this 1 1-day sadhna also requires, describing the combination as achieving "two tar gets with one arrow ."
12. Additional Dietary Rule: No Food After 6:00 PM

For these 1 1 days, practitioners should consume nothing but warm water after 6:00 PM. Per this teaching, this practice is expected to visibly improve a practitioner's complexion (tez, radiance), increase tapobal (spiritual potency from austerity), and increase grahan shakti (receptive capacity) — comparable to mountain-dwelling ascetics who subsist mainly on water .
13. No Turning Back Once Committed

Bhaiya reiterates that once this level of shakti is invoked on a practitioner's behalf, breaking the commitment is described as inviting real dif ficulty from those same invoked shaktis — practitioners are ur ged not to give up partway through.
14. Dir ect Access to Bhaiya for 1 1 Days

Practitioners are given direct access to message or call Bhaiya at any time, day or night, throughout the 1 1-day period, with a guarantee of a response — though Bhaiya specifically asks that this access not be used to say "I can't do this anymore," but rather to work through genuine dif ficulties together .
15. Why the Shaktis Being Sent This Time Are Mor e "Ugra" (Intense)

Bhaiya explains that the shaktis a practitioner has worked with up to this point have been comparatively gentle/for giving. The shaktis being invoked for this batch are more intense ("ugra") — described using the metaphor of previously carrying a light rod, now being handed a sword: a sword is inherently more dangerous, but for those who know how to wield it, it becomes a powerful tool rather than a hazard, and Bhaiya commits to helping practitioners learn to hold it safely .
16. Why the Rules Incr ease as Practitioners Advance

Per this teaching, as a practitioner draws closer to devta-level responsibility , the rules and discipline expected of them naturally increase — described as "protocol" tied directly to the increased responsibility and closeness to divine authority being granted, not as arbitrary restriction. Bhaiya compares this progression to becoming part of "Bhagwan Ram's army ," where increasing discipline is a mark of increasing trust, not punishment.
17. The Second Charan Jaap Method

The core jaap method for this batch is explained in detail: sit in asana, look into Prabhu's eyes, and mentally (not aloud) repeat "Ram Ram Ram..." with total focus on the name — closing the eyes when the mind wanders, refocusing on "Ram," then reopening the eyes to look again at Prabhu. The prayer should be of fered with humility (vinati), not ego (ahankar) — asking Prabhu to accept the practitioner fully ("tan man dhan se main aapka hoon"), to guide the way forward, and to allow direct connection and communication.
18. What Not to Ask For During This Jaap

Practitioners are specifically instructed not to ask for their drishti to be "taken" or further opened during this practice. Per this teaching, one's drishti is already exactly as open as it currently needs to be — deliberately trying to force it further open risks confusion (bhram) and illusory visions, potentially including disturbing false experiences (such as perceiving an attack that isn't real).
19. The Five Reasons a Practitioner Is Eligible for This Sadhna

Bhaiya explains that receiving access to this level of sadhna depends on five factors: (1) the bhakti, shakti, and ef fort of the mentors who brought the practitioner forward; (2) the practitioner's own tapasya (austerity/ef fort); (3) sant approval — sadhna is never granted without sant permission; (4) the practitioner's own purva janam (past-life) shakti, which actively seeks to be invoked; and (5) guru bal (the strength/grace of the guru lineage), with Hanuman ji's grace resting on all practitioners collectively .
20. A Preview: Futur e Surya Vigyan Teaching and Its Tests

Bhaiya previews that in a future teaching on "Surya Vigyan" (solar science), practitioners will face a stage where powerful forces (comparable to Hanuman ji's level) will directly test/"attack" their faith — and at that stage, only a practitioner's own purva janam shakti and mahasookshma sharir (referred to poetically as "Parikshit Bhaiya," i.e., one's own examined/tested subtle self) will be able to protect them, not external belief in mantra or Baba alone.
21. Bhaiya's Own Experience With This Same Sadhna

Bhaiya shares that when he himself first performed this exact sadhna, his early sessions showed him disturbing visions of unfamiliar , unpleasant lokas (not "fancy" or pleasant realms) that shook him deeply each time. Over successive days, the visions gradually revealed deeper truth, culminating in Baba showing him the actual "formation of Earth" — an experience so intense that he has still only taken

that particular "class" once. He notes that the day after that specific teaching, other practitioners' faith wavered and they experienced real dif ficulties/attacks, requiring their sankalp shakti to be re-invoked.
22. Self-Discovery Through the Sadhna

Bhaiya frames this sadhna as fundamentally a process of self-discovery — learning who one truly is beneath the surface. He notes that unusually strong emotional reactions (such as intense anger) that surface during this practice may reflect a practitioner's own past-life tattva resurfacing, and that such tendencies can be consciously changed if the practitioner chooses to work on them.
23. Continuing Other Practices During the 1 1 Days

Per this teaching, practitioners may continue other pre-existing spiritual or professional practices during the 1 1 days (for example, astrology readings performed as a livelihood) if genuinely necessary , though Bhaiya recommends pausing non-essential extra rituals (such as separate jal vidhi/tel vidhi practices) for these 1 1 days specifically , delegating them to someone else if needed. Ordinary daily activities — shaving, grooming, professional obligations — are explicitly permitted without restriction.
24. Flexibility for Practical Constraints

Per this teaching, practitioners with genuine physical constraints (for example, needing to sit in a chair rather than on the floor) may adapt their seating accordingly , and those already doing Siya Tattva sadhna on a given day should not additionally start this 1 1-day sadhna that same day — it should begin the next available day . If a practitioner wishes to also continue Siya Tattva sadhna alongside this 1 1-day sadhna, it requires a separate minimum one-hour session and does not count toward the four -hour minimum.
25. No Restriction for Women's Physical Cycles
Per this teaching, women experiencing their menstrual cycle during these 1 1 days face no restriction on participation.
26. The 18 Siddhis of Ram Sadhna

Bhaiya closes with a comparison: Bhagwan Krishna is traditionally described as possessing 16 kalas (arts/attainments), but Bhagwan Ram's sadhna is described as conferring 18 siddhis upon a genuine practitioner — described as the highest tattva attainable, with no higher tattva existing above it.
27. Why Bhagwan Ram Is Described as Very Strict

In response to a sangat member's question about why Bhagwan Ram is described as stricter than Hanuman ji despite both being revered, Bhaiya explains: Bhagwan Ram, as "Maryada Purushottam" (the ideal upholder of dharmic conduct/boundaries), always follows rules and protocol precisely , and the greater the responsibility and power held, the stricter the required discipline — illustrated with an analogy to Dubai's reputation for strict laws correlating directly with its reputation for safety . Hanuman ji, by contrast, primarily wields and channels Ram's power rather than holding ultimate authority himself, which is of fered as part of why he is experienced as comparatively gentler .
28. The Reward of Genuine Follow-Thr ough

Per this teaching, a practitioner who consistently follows through on what they commit to and say will find that their spoken word gradually gains real manifesting power — "jo aapne kaha wahi hoga" (what you say will come to pass) — but only for those who genuinely do what they say they will do; empty commitments do not gain this power .
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This session inducts the third batch of Ashaeiynn's Third Eye program with an 1 1-day sankalp; no partial or hesitant participation is accepted — commit fully or wait for a future batch. Minimum daily requirement: four hours of jaap, done strictly seated (never walking), which may be split into shorter seated segments. Physical setup: a photo of Prabhu before a lit diya, self-applied tilak with rice (chandan/itr/flowers optional), looking into Prabhu's eyes while chanting, a personally-cleaned dedicated space used by no one else, and sleeping on the ground for the full 1 1 days (out of respect for visiting sants). No food after 6:00 PM — warm water only — to increase radiance, tapobal, and receptive capacity . The second charan jaap method: mentally repeat "Ram Ram Ram," alternating gaze into Prabhu's eyes with closed-eye refocusing, of fered with humility rather than ego, and explicitly without asking for one's own drishti to be further opened (risk of confusion/illusion). Five conditions make a practitioner eligible for this sadhna: mentors' bhakti/shakti, the practitioner's own tapasya, sant approval, purva janam shakti, and guru bal (with Hanuman ji's grace on all). A future "Surya Vigyan" teaching will involve powerful forces testing practitioners' faith directly — protection at that stage comes only from one's own purva janam shakti and mahasookshma sharir . Bhagwan Ram's sadhna is described as conferring 18 siddhis (compared to Krishna's traditional 16 kalas) — the highest tattva described in this framework. Ram is described as stricter than Hanuman ji specifically because greater responsibility and power require greater discipline (the "Dubai" analogy: strict rules correlate with safety). Genuine follow-through on commitments is described as the basis for one's spoken word gaining real manifesting power over time. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .

Bot Response Guidelines

Present the 1 1-day sadhna's specific practical rules (four -hour minimum, seated posture only , ground-sleeping, no food after 6 PM, personally-cleaned dedicated space) precisely , since these are concrete instructions given to enrolled practitioners, not general guidance for all users. Keep the explicit instruction not to ask for one's own drishti to be further opened intact and precise — this is a specific caution against a specific risk (confusion/illusion), not a general statement that drishti should never develop. Preserve the distinction between Ram's 18 siddhis and Krishna's traditional 16 kalas as this teaching's own comparative framework, not a claim about the deities' relative greatness overall. Keep the "strictness = responsibility" framing (illustrated by the Dubai analogy) intact when explaining why Ram is described as stricter than Hanuman ji — this is of fered as an explanation of protocol, not a value judgment between the two. Present Bhaiya's own account of his early sadhna experience (disturbing visions, the "formation of Earth" class, other practitioners' subsequent faith wavering) as his personal testimony specific to this teaching, not as a guaranteed outcome for every practitioner . Note that eligibility for this level of sadhna depends on five specific factors (mentors' ef fort, practitioner's tapasya, sant approval, purva janam shakti, guru bal) — do not present it as available to anyone without these conditions. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
